questions.q: According to the lecture, which trimester of infection generally gives the worst outcome, with the exception of HSV?

options.e: Wrong. Early infection, when organs form, is worse.
Wrong. Third-trimester infection is generally less damaging, except HSV.
Wrong. The lecture singles out the first trimester.
Correct. With the exception of HSV, infections during the first trimester have the worst outcome.

questions.q: A neonate is infected at birth by the herpes virus. Which type is most often responsible, and why?

options.t: HSV-1, because it predominantly causes genital infection
options.e: Wrong. HSV-2 is the predominant genital type.

options.t: HSV-2, because it is transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes
options.e: Wrong. HSV is not mosquito-borne.

options.t: HSV-1, because it is acquired from the placenta only
options.e: Wrong. Newborn disease is mostly acquired from the genital tract.

options.t: HSV-2, because it predominantly causes genital infection
options.e: Correct. Newborns usually acquire HSV-2 from the maternal genital tract.

questions.q: In which situation is rubella infection common, according to the lecture?

options.t: In countries with universal maternal screening
options.e: Wrong. Screening is not what drives rubella prevalence.

options.t: Only in tropical regions with Aedes mosquitoes
options.e: Wrong. Rubella is not mosquito-borne.

options.t: In countries where mothers are unvaccinated
options.e: Correct. Rubella remains common where maternal vaccination is lacking.
Wrong. Seasonality is mentioned for fifth disease.

questions.q: Approximately what proportion of all congenital anomalies is attributed to perinatal infections?

options.e: Wrong. This is too high.
Wrong. This is the Zika transmission rate with maternal infection.
Wrong. This is too high.
Correct. About 2% to 3% of congenital anomalies are attributed to perinatal infections.

questions.q: Which list contains only the 'Other' infections named under TORCH in this lecture?

options.e: Wrong. Measles is among 'other viruses now known', not the listed O group.
Correct. These are the 'Other' infections named in the lecture.
Wrong. CMV is the C of TORCH.
Wrong. Rubella is the R of TORCH.

questions.q: Which virus is NOT listed among the other viruses now known to cause congenital infections?

options.e: Wrong. It is listed.
Correct. It is not listed; the list includes West Nile, measles, enteroviruses, hepatitis E, adenovirus, LCMV and Zika.
Wrong. It is listed.
Wrong. It is listed.

questions.q: A mother with untreated syphilis delivers a baby who is asymptomatic at birth. Within what period can symptoms appear?

options.t: Only within the first week of life
options.e: Wrong. Symptoms may develop up to two years.

options.t: Only after five years of age
options.e: Wrong. Symptoms develop in the first two years.
Wrong. Infants are frequently asymptomatic at birth.

options.t: At any time during the first two years of life
options.e: Correct. Infants are often asymptomatic at birth, with symptoms developing during the first two years.

questions.q: Which description fits Treponema pallidum?

options.t: Spirochete and strict human pathogen surviving in warm, moist sites
options.e: Correct. It survives in genitalia, mucous membranes and bloodstream.
Wrong. It is a spirochete.

options.t: Enveloped RNA virus carried by Aedes mosquitoes
options.e: Wrong. This describes Zika virus.

options.t: Single-stranded DNA virus infecting erythroid progenitors
options.e: Wrong. This describes parvovirus B19.

questions.q: An infant has mucopurulent rhinitis, desquamating maculopapular skin lesions, hepatosplenomegaly and jaundice. What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.e: Wrong. This causes a slapped-cheek rash and anemia.
Wrong. This is defined by microcephaly.
Correct. These are typical features, with bone abnormalities also seen.
Wrong. This has skin lesions with cataracts and neurological defects.

questions.q: What is the treatment of choice for congenital syphilis, and the main infection-control measure?

options.t: Penicillin; screening and treating pregnant women
options.e: Correct. Antibiotics, typically penicillin, plus antenatal screening and treatment.

options.t: Acyclovir; screening and treating pregnant women
options.e: Wrong. Acyclovir is used for VZV.
Wrong. Mosquito control applies to Zika.

options.t: Supportive care only; good hand hygiene
options.e: Wrong. Syphilis is treated with antibiotics.

questions.q: Which are recognized complications of congenital syphilis?

options.t: Microcephaly in all cases, seizures and feeding difficulty
options.e: Wrong. This describes congenital Zika syndrome.

options.t: Neurosyphilis, blindness, deafness and developmental delay
options.e: Correct. These are the complications listed.
Wrong. This is fifth disease.

options.t: Cataracts, cerebellar atrophy and cutaneous scarring
options.e: Wrong. These are features of congenital VZV syndrome.

questions.q: A pregnant woman has a 'slapped cheek' rash with swelling and redness on her arms and legs. Which agent is responsible and which cells does it infect?

options.e: Wrong. It targets erythroid progenitors.

options.t: Parvovirus B19; erythroid progenitor cells in bone marrow
options.e: Correct. It causes anemia and rashes, and is a single-stranded DNA virus of Parvoviridae.
Wrong. Slapped cheek is caused by parvovirus B19.

options.t: Varicella-zoster virus; dorsal root ganglion cells
options.e: Wrong. VZV remains dormant there but does not cause slapped cheek.

questions.q: What is the main management of congenital fifth disease?

options.e: Wrong. This is for syphilis.

questions.q: When is the incidence of fifth disease highest?

options.e: Wrong. Incidence is highest in winter and spring.

options.e: Wrong. It affects people of all ages.

questions.q: What is the genome and family of varicella-zoster virus?

options.e: Wrong. This is parvovirus B19.
Wrong. This is Zika virus.

questions.q: A newborn has skin lesions, cataracts, microcephaly and cerebellar atrophy. The mother had chickenpox in pregnancy. Which treatment reduces fetal transmission if given to the mother?

options.e: Correct. Acyclovir can treat primary maternal infection and reduce fetal transmission.
Wrong. This is for syphilis.

questions.q: How can VZV be transmitted?

options.t: Airborne droplets, contact with skin lesions, or across the placenta

questions.q: A newborn from Brazil has microcephaly, seizures and feeding difficulty. What is the causative agent's classification?

options.e: Wrong. This is parvovirus B19.

questions.q: What is the transmission rate with maternal Zika infection in pregnancy, and what are the main preventive measures?

options.t: 30% to 70%; mosquito control, safe sex, donor blood screening
options.e: Correct. There is no specific treatment or vaccine.
Wrong. Penicillin is for syphilis.

questions.q: What is the main route of Zika virus transmission to humans?

options.e: Wrong. This is a route for VZV.

options.e: Correct. It can also be transmitted congenitally, sexually, by transfusion and by laboratory exposure.
